Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zujose 0.0.0.9000

  • jwt_decode() unwraps one level of nesting only, a signed JWT inside a JWE, with a separate allow-list for each layer: decrypt for the JWE, and key and algorithms for the signature. A signed JWT inside a signed JWT is now refused with zujose_policy_error, on its header and before any signature is checked; call jws_verify() on each layer to accept one (#46).

  • jwt_decode() checks a JWE’s key management against decrypt’s algorithms before the rule for encrypted-only JWTs, so an unknown or disallowed alg gets the allow-list error. An unknown alg was refused as an encrypted-only JWT with public-key key management (#77).

  • Every zujose_argument_error names the function the caller called, such as jwt_encode() rather than the jws_sign() it calls, and every argument is checked before the token is read: jwt_decode() reported a bad token before a bad decrypt, limits or key, and jws_verify() and jwe_decrypt() before a bad key, payload or limits (#75).

  • A caller’s header or unprotected member of the wrong type, such as jws_sign(..., header = list(typ = 1)), is a zujose_argument_error on every encoder: jws_sign(), jws_signer(), jwt_encode(), jwe_encrypt() and jwe_recipient(). It was a zujose_parse_error, the class for a malformed token, or was raised only when signing (#148).

  • A key argument of the wrong R type is a zujose_argument_error, as ?zujose_error now states once: a mistake in the caller’s own code is an argument error, and anything wrong with a token is a token error. jwk_oct(1), jwk_set(1), jwk_thumbprint(1), as_jwk(123), a key that is not a jwk (or, when verifying or decrypting, a jwk_set or function), and jwk_generate()’s kty, crv, alg and size of the wrong type or out of their range raised zujose_key_error. A malformed or too weak key is still a zujose_key_error (#78).

  • jws_verify() refuses a flattened or general JWS without a payload member, given no payload argument, with zujose_parse_error. It verified the token over the empty payload. An empty payload member is still the empty payload, and the compact serialization is unchanged (#147).

  • zujose_info() and zujose_unsupported_error name zucrypt 0.1.1 as the version every algorithm needs. zucrypt re-planned its releases, and 0.1.1 now carries all the primitives zujose uses beyond HMAC and AES-CBC, randomness and SHA-2 included. They named 0.3.0, 0.4.0 and 0.5.0, which will not carry them.

  • as_jwk_set() skips a member of keys that is not a JSON object, as RFC 7517 section 5 has it. A string member was read as JWK text or as PEM (#44).

  • A JSON null in a JWS or JWE JSON serialization is no longer read as an absent member. A null header, unprotected, protected or encrypted_key, or a null kid, typ or cty header, let a token verify or decrypt; each is now a zujose_parse_error. Found by the differential fuzzer in tools/fuzz/ (#144).

  • A header, JWS JSON token or claims set nested more than about 800 levels deep, which zujson parses up to 1000, no longer exhausts the C stack: the check for repeated member names and the claims comparison walk the value level by level instead of recursing (#141).

  • jwt_decode() refuses a JWT with an unencoded payload (b64: false), outer or nested, with zujose_policy_error before any key is tried (RFC 7797 section 7). It returned the claims (#126).

  • jwt_decode() refuses an exp, nbf or iat beyond any time POSIXct can represent, such as 1e308, with zujose_parse_error. It returned the claim as an NA time. jwt_encode() refuses such a time, from claims, expires_in or not_before, with zujose_argument_error, so it no longer writes a token jwt_decode() refuses (#127).

  • jwt_decode() and jwt_decoder() refuse repeated, NA or empty names in claims with zujose_argument_error. Only the first of two expectations for one claim was checked (#118).

  • Expectations in jwt_decode(claims = ) compare JSON values, not JSON text: object members may come in any order. NA and non-finite numbers are refused rather than matching null, and NULL expects null. exp, nbf and iat are compared, and passed to a function, as the POSIXct times jwt_decode() returns. ?jwt_decode says how vectors and arrays match (#128).

  • jose_peek() gives NULL for payload and signing_input on a compact detached JWS, as it does for a flattened one. It gave raw(0) and the header followed by "." (#131).

  • ?jwe_encrypt documents that other JOSE implementations cap PBES2 p2c when they decrypt (jwcrypto at 16 384, JavaScript’s jose at 10 000), so a token for them needs header = list(p2c = 10000) or less. The default stays 600 000 (#140).

  • jwt_encode() documents key as one jwk, and refuses jws_signer()s with a clear zujose_argument_error: a JWT is compact and has one signature. It inherited a list-of-signers key from jws_sign() that its own default header made it refuse (#130).

  • Errors that escaped as base R, zucrypt or zujson conditions are now zujose_errors: an enc that is not one string in jwe_encrypt(), a NUL byte in an unencoded (b64 = FALSE) payload, an RSA size that is not a multiple of 8 in jwk_generate() (now documented), a bad index in [[ on a jwk_set, and a PBES2 p2c beyond 2^32 - 1, which is a parse error even under jose_limits(p2c = Inf) (#123).

  • Names on R arguments no longer change the JSON zujose writes or the values it compares. A named expires_in, not_before, exp, nbf, iat, p2c, alg, enc, kid, typ or registered claim was written as an object, a named list of jws_signer()s wrote signatures as an object, and a named issuer or subject in jwt_decode() never matched (#120).

  • jwe_encrypt() and jwe_recipient() refuse zip in every header with zujose_argument_error. In unprotected or a recipient’s header it was written over content that was never compressed (#117).

  • jwe_encrypt() refuses a jwe_recipient() header alg that disagrees with the recipient’s algorithm, in every format, as jws_sign() does. It was silently replaced in the general serialization (#129).

  • jws_sign(), jws_signer(), jwe_encrypt(), jwe_recipient() and jwt_encode() refuse, with zujose_argument_error, a header or claims set with a repeated, NA or empty name at any depth, a member given in more than one header, a data frame or unnamed list as the claims set, and a value JSON cannot represent, such as a raw or complex vector. A repeated header member was dropped and a nested one written, giving tokens zujose’s own decoder refuses (#119, #123).

  • Header members and key members are read by their exact names. A p2count header member no longer sets the PBES2 iteration count, and a kidnap header no longer prints as the key’s kid (#122).

  • Printing a key of an unknown kty says “unknown key type” instead of “needs zucrypt (>= NA)” (#136).

  • [ on a jwk_set refuses an NA or out-of-range index with zujose_argument_error, instead of making a set that holds NULL and cannot be printed (#135).

  • jwk_public(), and so jwk_json() without private, maps a private key’s key_ops to its public half’s: sign to verify, decrypt to encrypt and unwrapKey to wrapKey. The public half of a signing key could not verify. With no public operation left, key_ops is dropped (#133).

  • jwk_generate("oct") accepts every oct algorithm jwk_oct() does: a PBES2-* password (256 bits by default), and a dir key named by its content encryption, such as alg = "A128GCM", made at that algorithm’s exact size (#132).

  • A JWK’s key_ops must be an array of strings; a JSON object is a key error. A present empty array permits no operation, and stays empty when written and read back, where before it meant no restriction. A list built in R may give key_ops as a character vector (#121).

  • as_jwk() refuses an RSA JWK with oth, private or public: zujose has no multi-prime keys (#125).

  • as_jwk() refuses a key whose members are not in their one canonical form: an RSA member with a leading zero octet, or an EC or X25519 x, y or d that is not exactly the curve’s length. Such a key had a different thumbprint from the same key written canonically. An ECDH-ES epk is held to the same rule (#94).

  • as_jwk() refuses a private X25519 JWK whose x is not the public key of its d (#124).

  • Printing jose_limits() no longer warns in a session whose OutDec is a comma (#137).

  • The default token limit of jose_limits() is 2 MiB, up from 1 MiB, so a token whose payload is at the default 1 MiB payload limit can be read. token bounds the encoded form, about 4/3 of the payload. Encoders do not check the limits (#134).

  • jws_verify() counts limits$keys across all of a general JWS’s signatures, not per signature, as jwe_decrypt() does. It checks every signature’s algorithm and keys before verifying any (#92).

  • The header and payload limits of jose_limits() are exact in bytes for Base64url parts. Before, a limit of n let up to two more bytes through in a compact or JSON JWS and in a JWE ciphertext (#91).

  • jws_sign() refuses b64 and crit in header or unprotected; the b64 argument sets them. A caller’s b64: false header with an encoded payload gave a token that verified as the wrong bytes (#72).

  • jwe_decrypt() counts limits$keys across all of a token’s recipients, not per recipient, so a JWE with many PBES2 or RSA recipients cannot multiply the key-derivation work (#37).

  • jws_verify() and jwt_decode() skip a key in a set that is too weak for the token’s algorithm, such as a legacy 1024-bit RSA key in a provider’s JWKS, instead of failing on it. A set with only weak keys is still a zujose_key_error (#39).

  • Argument errors, such as a wrong type, an out-of-range limit or format = "compact" with several recipients, now raise zujose_argument_error, a zujose_error, instead of a plain error (#40).

  • jwt_decode() refuses an encrypted-only JWT whose key management is public-key (RSA-OAEP*, RSA1_5, ECDH-ES*), because anyone holding the recipient’s public key could have made it. Its claims must come inside a signed JWT (cty: "JWT"). Encrypted-only JWTs with symmetric key management are still accepted (#34).

  • Functions are named after the object they work on: jwt_encode(), jwt_decode() and jwt_decoder(); jws_sign(), jws_signer() and jws_verify(); jwe_encrypt(), jwe_recipient(), jwe_decrypt() and jwe_decryption(); jwk_oct(), jwk_generate(), as_jwk(), jwk_set(), as_jwk_set(), jwk_public(), jwk_json(), jwk_pem(), jwk_with_kid() and jwk_thumbprint(). They replace the jose_ names of the development version; jose_peek() and jose_limits() keep theirs. Classes follow: jwk, jwk_set, jws_verified, jwe_decrypted, jwt_claims.

  • Documentation: a README, and three articles on the package website: Get started, migrating from jose, and verifying tokens against a provider’s JWKS with a caching resolver. The key help pages explain how secrets are held in R memory.

  • jwk_generate("oct") accepts 128-bit keys when no alg is given, or for dir, as documented; it required 256 bits (#30).

  • The package, developed as zujwt, is renamed zujose, the name of its design: conditions are zujose_* and zujwt_info() is zujose_info().

  • Condition classes for every error the package will raise, all inheriting from zujose_error (?zujose_error).

  • jose_peek() reads a JWS or JWE in the compact, flattened or general JSON serialization, without verifying it, and returns every part decoded: its headers; for a JWS, its payload, claims, signatures and signing inputs; for a JWE, its encrypted keys, IV, ciphertext, tag and AAD.

  • jose_limits() sets the resource limits every token is checked against before anything is decoded.

  • Keys: jwk_oct() makes a symmetric key, as_jwk() reads a JWK, jwk_json() writes one, jwk_public() strips private members, and jwk_thumbprint() computes RFC 7638 thumbprints and RFC 9278 thumbprint URIs. jwk_with_kid() sets kid, by default to the thumbprint. RSA, EC and OKP keys are read and kept but cannot be used yet.

  • Key sets: jwk_set() and as_jwk_set(), with [[ selecting by kid. Malformed entries in a JWK Set are ignored, as RFC 7517 asks.

  • jws_sign() and jws_verify() sign and verify JWS with HS256, HS384 and HS512, in all three serializations, with several signers through jws_signer(), detached payloads, and RFC 7797 unencoded payloads. jws_verify() needs algorithms, has no way to accept none, and refuses a key that does not fit the token’s algorithm.

  • zujose_info() lists every JOSE algorithm and whether this installation can use it.

  • jwt_encode() and jwt_decode() sign and check JWTs. Decoding checks exp, nbf, iat, max_age, iss, sub, aud, typ, required claims, per-claim expectations and a validate hook in one call; exp is required by default. Each failure has its own condition class under zujose_claim_error. jwt_decoder() fixes a policy once and returns a checking function.

  • jwe_decrypt() decrypts JWE with dir, A128KW, A192KW and A256KW key management and A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 and A256CBC-HS512 content encryption, in all three serializations and for several recipients. Every decryption failure raises one class with one message. Compressed (zip) tokens are refused.

  • jwe_encrypt() encrypts to one recipient, or to several through jwe_recipient(), with the same algorithms. Every message gets a fresh content encryption key and IV from the operating system’s random source, which cannot be supplied by the caller.

  • JWE gains A128GCM, A192GCM and A256GCM content encryption, and A128GCMKW, A192GCMKW, A256GCMKW and the three PBES2-* key management algorithms, over zucrypt’s AES-GCM and PBKDF2. A PBES2 token whose p2c exceeds jose_limits()$p2c, or whose p2s is shorter than 8 bytes, is refused before any key is derived. A dir key whose alg names the content encryption, as in RFC 7520 section 5.6, is accepted.

  • RSA: RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384 and PS512 signatures, and RSA-OAEP and RSA-OAEP-256 key management. RSA1_5 decrypts only when algorithms names it, never encrypts, and fails like a wrong key when its padding is bad. RSA keys are read from JWKs (with all CRT parameters for a private key) and from PEM, written with the new jwk_pem(), generated with jwk_generate("RSA"), and must be at least 2048 bits to be used.

  • Elliptic curves: ES256, ES384 and ES512 signatures (raw r || s), and ECDH-ES, ECDH-ES+A128KW, ECDH-ES+A192KW and ECDH-ES+A256KW key agreement on P-256, P-384, P-521 and X25519, with the Concat KDF of RFC 7518. An ephemeral key that is malformed or off its curve is a parse error, and one on another curve than the key a key error, before any key agreement. EC and X25519 keys are read from JWKs and PEM, written by jwk_pem() and generated by jwk_generate("EC") and ("OKP"). Ed25519 keys are read and kept but cannot be used.

  • jwk_generate() makes a random oct key, sized for its alg. RSA, EC and OKP generation names the zucrypt version it needs.

  • jwt_encode(jti = TRUE) adds a random 128-bit jti.

  • zujose now needs the development version of zucrypt, for crypt_rand_bytes(), crypt_aes_gcm_encrypt() and crypt_pbkdf2(). zujose_info() reports an algorithm available when the installed zucrypt exports what it needs, so a development zucrypt counts.

  • jwt_decode() accepts a JWT sent as a JWE only with decrypt = jwe_decryption(...).
